items.title: Sal Gutierrez Interview, 1970-01-15
items.q: The interviewee discusses 'Buzzy Willow' and 'Harry Shields' in detail, but when the interviewer corrects/clarifies 'Not Williamson', the interviewee does not mention Williamson again or attribute any relationship to them.

ctx.x: I didn't get into the job. I said, Goppsen, oh, he's a great drummer. Which he is. But the guy said, he got a break with B-Funk. I mean, the guy's a top-knop musician, man. He can play with anybody. How much did they pay at the fern? I'm always wondering. Well, I'll tell you that story, too. I'll give it to you straight. A nickel? A nickel? No, man. They didn't Father Goppsen, because poor man's dead, man. This Father Billy Gillen. He played just like Bakesh Pounder back then. He played trumpet. He was in the…

Buzzy Willow. The band-jole player. Yeah, the band-jole player. Well, the job was ready to play, paid forty dollars a week, see? Which was bad in those days. Forty weeks, see? But each leader, when they cut everybody down, see? If the guy was very good, you know, I'd pay him a little more, such as Harry Shields, you know, I'd give Harry a little more, cut the drummer down a little more, see? And so on, you know, that's how it worked, you see? My mom gave it to you straight. So when Bill was there, I got forty…
